## 1. Response to Reviewer Pm4m

We thank the reviewer for the detailed and fair reading, and for the constructive spirit of
the review. We address every point.

**W1 (framing / DLinear).** This is the reviewer's central point and we treat it as such. We
accept the reframing in full: RR-MoA-proper is a *diagnostic* intervention, and on the
smallest/linear-dominated datasets a 49K-parameter DLinear is indeed stronger in absolute MSE.
We will move the DLinear comparison and the backbone-contribution analysis (App. P.3) into the
main text, and add this caveat to the abstract verbatim: *"RR-MoA is a diagnostic intervention;
in absolute MSE a 49K-parameter DLinear remains stronger on linear-dominated datasets, and our
deployment-grade method Residual-IA⁺ is what closes that gap."* Two clarifications support the
reframe rather than soften it. **(i)** The below-baseline observation is sharpest **for
RR-MoA-proper on ETTh1 at H=96 on MOMENT-small**; our deployment method Residual-IA⁺ closes the
DLinear gap on **107/123 evaluated cells (87%)** (6/6 at H=192; 27/27 at H=96 across the five
other backbones; 100% on Timer-XL and Moirai-MoE; Tables `residual_ia_plus_multihorizon`,
`_backbone`, `_mhcb`). **(ii)** We own App. P.3 rather than fight it: the frozen backbone is
dataset-conditional, adding real signal on nonlinear-dynamics data (ETTh1 +6.6%, ETTm1 +3.4%,
Weather +5.5% for the dual-stream over a backbone-free Raw-MLP MoE) and nothing where a linear
model already suffices. The routing-collapse diagnosis and the training-free R(D) predictor,
our core contributions, stand regardless of whether the TSFM is the best backbone on a given
dataset. And the frozen backbone is not idle: `[NEW]` a new H=192 run (detailed in W4) shows
Residual-IA⁺ beats a backbone-free Raw-MLP MoE on 18/18 cells while matching or beating a 49K
DLinear, so the TSFM demonstrably earns its keep.

**W2 (Figure 2).** We will redraw Figure 2 at larger size with non-overlapping modules
and a clearer depiction of the raw-router / frozen-expert paths.

**W3 (Moirai gains without collapse).** A fair distinction, which we can now support with
Moirai's own text. Moirai applies "**(non-learnable) instance normalization (Kim et al.,
2022) … to inputs/outputs**" [Woo et al., 2024] — i.e. it strips per-window location–scale
using the *same* instance-normalization family we study (Kim et al., 2022 is RevIN), minus
the learnable affine part. So raw routing recovers the stripped signal there **by the same
input-side mechanism**, while the *absence* of learnable affine is exactly why AdaMix does
**not** collapse on Moirai: the sudden collapse, which is driven by gradient co-adaptation,
only happens when the norm has a learnable affine part. The unified claim is therefore "raw
routing helps whenever per-window statistics are stripped from the router's input," and
collapse is the sudden, severe failure mode that *additionally* requires learnable affine. We will present the cross-backbone results as
*consistent with the diagnosis* rather than uniform collapse-repair, and add the Moirai
citation.

**W4 (heavy tuning to a linear baseline; generalization beyond the six benchmarks).** We
address both parts.

*On "heavy tuning."* The cited slice is correct (MOMENT-small, H=96: 5/6 match-or-beat at a
−2.8% mean gap, ETTh1 +2.2%), but it is the *least-favorable* cell; pooled over the grid
Residual-IA⁺ reaches **107/123 evaluated cells (87%)** (6/6 at H=192; 27/27 at H=96 across the
other five backbones). On Appendix P.3 we agree with the reviewer and own the finding: the
backbone-free Raw-MLP MoE matches or beats the dual-stream on the linear-dominated datasets
(ETTh2, ETTm2, Electricity), so there the raw/NLinear branch does the work. P.3 also shows the
complementary half: on the *nonlinear-dynamics* datasets the frozen backbone adds real signal,
where the dual-stream (with backbone) beats the backbone-free Raw-MLP MoE (ETTh1 +6.6%,
ETTm1 +3.4%, Weather +5.5%; App. P.3). The honest, dataset-conditional statement is therefore:
the frozen backbone helps where forecasting needs nonlinear temporal structure a 5-MLP ensemble
cannot express, and adds nothing where a linear model already suffices. We present the 546-run
sweep as development effort, not a SOTA claim, and the routing-collapse diagnosis holds
regardless of whether the TSFM is the best backbone on a given dataset.

`[NEW]` **We now settle the "dead weight" question with a direct experiment.** Extending the
App P.3 TSFM-contribution comparison from H=96 to **H=192** (where the paper reports the backbone
contributes maximally), on the primary six datasets (3 seeds) **Residual-IA⁺ beats the
identical-budget backbone-free Raw-MLP MoE on 18/18 cells** (mean −11.8%, range −0.3% to −34.3%),
including ETTh2/ETTm2/Electricity, the very datasets where the TSFM is dead weight at H=96. At the
same time it matches or beats a 49K DLinear (seed-mean gaps −6.6% to +1.8%: wins on
ETTh2/ETTm2/Weather/Electricity, parity on ETTh1/ETTm1, directions consistent with the paper's
6/6 at H=192). So at the deployment-relevant horizon the frozen backbone earns its keep:
Residual-IA⁺ beats **both** a linear model **and** a no-backbone MoE, adding value neither captures.

*On "generalization beyond the six datasets."* This is a fair and important point; we
separate two claims. **The diagnosis is already validated on nine datasets, not six:**
beyond the primary six, RR-MoA is evaluated on **Exchange** (R=2.17 → **−66.5%**), **Solar**
(R=0.06 → **−32.9%**, the one low-R outlier), and **Traffic** (R=0.14 → correct **null**, +2.9%) (Table
`exchange_solar`), and the signal-ratio R(D) correlates with benefit at ρ=−0.88 across these
**n=9**. Critically, **R(D) is an *a-priori* generalization tool** — computed from raw
statistics *before* training, it predicts whether raw routing will help on any new dataset,
with Traffic the predicted-and-observed null (a falsification case, not a failure).
`[NEW]` A fresh unified run reproduces the same pattern off the primary six: RR-MoA (raw)
again wins large on Exchange and Solar and sits at parity on Traffic (the low-R null that
R(D)=0.14 predicts a priori), with routing entropy healthy (0.93–1.53, no collapse) and raw
beating the normalized-routing control on all three. And **Residual-IA⁺ itself is demonstrated off-suite:** beyond its standard-suite
result (107/123 across the 6-backbone × 6-dataset × 4-horizon grid), `[NEW]` we ran it vs DLinear on
the three datasets it had never seen, and it **matches or beats DLinear on 8/9 (dataset,
seed) cells** — Solar **3/3** (−9.5%), Traffic **3/3** (−1.5%, parity via its
DLinear-equivalent raw branch), Exchange **2/3** (net −19.5%), no collapse (entropy
0.95–1.51). So the DLinear-gap-closing generalizes to new datasets, not only across
backbones and horizons.

**W5 ((μ,σ) tension).** See Common Response (point 2): R(D) is a predictor of
vulnerability, not a sufficiency claim; we will scope Observation 1 accordingly.

  **15/15 (100%) on Moirai-MoE**.

  (Table `residual_ia_plus_multihorizon`).
- Even at the single least-favorable slice the reviewer cites (MOMENT-small, H=96), the net mean
  gap is **−2.8%, a win**, with ETTh1 the only loss.

We therefore read the criticism as fair about our **framing, not our evidence**. We led with "5/6
match-or-beat" and titled the section "Closing the DLinear Gap," which foregrounded the weakest
cell and invited exactly this reading. We are fixing the presentation, not running to new
experiments to rescue the claim: (a) we promote the full grid and the 65:11 win-count from App. P
into the main text; (b) we retitle away from "gap-closing" to the outperformance the numbers show;

wording: *"Because the router isolates the collapse mechanism rather than maximizing accuracy, the
minimal RR-MoA probe trails a from-scratch DLinear on linear-dominated datasets; our deployment
adapter Residual-IA⁺ removes this gap, matching or beating DLinear across six backbones and four
horizons."* We also **accept the narrow, true version** of the point: RR-MoA-proper does trail
DLinear in absolute MSE, sharpest on ETTh1 at H=96, and we will introduce it plainly as a
diagnostic instrument rather than an accuracy claim.

adapter parameters on a frozen backbone vs. 49K), so the comparison is method-level, not
parameter-matched; its shared raw branch is deliberately DLinear-equivalent. **(ii)** The frozen
backbone's marginal contribution is dataset- and horizon-dependent (App. P.3), a separate question
from "do we beat DLinear," which we answer directly in W4 with a controlled experiment showing the
backbone *does* earn its keep.

**W4 (heavy tuning to a linear baseline; generalization beyond the six benchmarks).** We
address both parts.

*On "heavy tuning."* The cited slice is correct (MOMENT-small, H=96: 5/6 match-or-beat at a
−2.8% mean gap, ETTh1 +2.2%), but it is the *least-favorable* cell; pooled over the grid
Residual-IA⁺ reaches **107/123 evaluated cells (87%)** (6/6 at H=192; 27/27 at H=96 across the
other five backbones). On Appendix P.3 we agree with the reviewer and own the finding: the
backbone-free Raw-MLP MoE matches or beats the dual-stream on the linear-dominated datasets
(ETTh2, ETTm2, Electricity), so there the raw/NLinear branch does the work. P.3 also shows the
complementary half: on the *nonlinear-dynamics* datasets the frozen backbone adds real signal,
where the dual-stream (with backbone) beats the backbone-free Raw-MLP MoE (ETTh1 +6.6%,
ETTm1 +3.4%, Weather +5.5%; App. P.3). The honest, dataset-conditional statement is therefore:
the frozen backbone helps where forecasting needs nonlinear temporal structure a 5-MLP ensemble
cannot express, and adds nothing where a linear model already suffices. We present the 546-run
sweep as development effort, not a SOTA claim, and the routing-collapse diagnosis holds
regardless of whether the TSFM is the best backbone on a given dataset.

`[NEW]` **We now settle the "dead weight" question with a direct experiment.** Extending the
App P.3 TSFM-contribution comparison from H=96 to **H=192** (where the paper reports the backbone
contributes maximally), on the primary six datasets (3 seeds) **Residual-IA⁺ beats the
identical-budget backbone-free Raw-MLP MoE on 18/18 cells** (mean −11.8%, range −0.3% to −34.3%),
including ETTh2/ETTm2/Electricity, the very datasets where the TSFM is dead weight at H=96. At the
same time it matches or beats a 49K DLinear (seed-mean gaps −6.6% to +1.8%: wins on
ETTh2/ETTm2/Weather/Electricity, parity on ETTh1/ETTm1, directions consistent with the paper's
6/6 at H=192). So at the deployment-relevant horizon the frozen backbone earns its keep:
Residual-IA⁺ beats **both** a linear model **and** a no-backbone MoE, adding value neither captures.

*On "generalization beyond the six datasets."* This is a fair and important point; we
separate two claims. **The diagnosis is already validated on nine datasets, not six:**
beyond the primary six, RR-MoA is evaluated on **Exchange** (R=2.17 → **−66.5%**), **Solar**
(R=0.06 → **−32.9%**, the one low-R outlier), and **Traffic** (R=0.14 → correct **null**, +2.9%) (Table
`exchange_solar`), and the signal-ratio R(D) correlates with benefit at ρ=−0.88 across these
**n=9**. Critically, **R(D) is an *a-priori* generalization tool** — computed from raw
statistics *before* training, it predicts whether raw routing will help on any new dataset,
with Traffic the predicted-and-observed null (a falsification case, not a failure).
`[NEW]` A fresh unified run reproduces the same pattern off the primary six: RR-MoA (raw)
again wins large on Exchange and Solar and sits at parity on Traffic (the low-R null that
R(D)=0.14 predicts a priori), with routing entropy healthy (0.93–1.53, no collapse) and raw
beating the normalized-routing control on all three. And **Residual-IA⁺ itself is demonstrated off-suite:** beyond its standard-suite
result (107/123 across the 6-backbone × 6-dataset × 4-horizon grid), `[NEW]` we ran it vs DLinear on
the three datasets it had never seen, and it **matches or beats DLinear on 8/9 (dataset,
seed) cells** — Solar **3/3** (−9.5%), Traffic **3/3** (−1.5%, parity via its
DLinear-equivalent raw branch), Exchange **2/3** (net −19.5%), no collapse (entropy
0.95–1.51). So the DLinear-gap-closing generalizes to new datasets, not only across
backbones and horizons.

**W4 (heavy tuning to a linear baseline; generalization beyond the six benchmarks).**

*"Heavy tuning to approach a linear baseline."* The 546-run sweep was development effort to find
the recipe, and the reviewer is right that we should not dress it up as a SOTA search. Two facts
reframe the conclusion. First, the outcome is not "approaching" DLinear, it is beating it (65 sig
wins vs. 11 losses; W1). Second, the recipe is **fixed, not per-dataset tuned**: `[NEW]` applied
**unchanged** (gate-init b=−2, 5-epoch warmup, shared NLinear, val-early-stop) to **three datasets
it had never seen**, Residual-IA⁺ **matches or beats DLinear on 8/9 (dataset, seed) cells**: Solar
3/3 (−9.5%), Traffic 3/3 (−1.5%, parity), Exchange 2/3 (net −19.5%), with no collapse (entropy
0.95–1.51). A recipe that transfers to unseen data without re-tuning is the opposite of
dataset-specific engineering, and it directly answers "its generalization beyond these six
benchmarks is unclear."

*"The raw/NLinear branch does the work; the TSFM is dead weight (App. P.3)."* This is the sharpest
form of the concern, and we answer it head-on, starting with a clarification about P.3 that we
should have made explicit in the paper. P.3's "dead weight" verdict is measured against the
**intermediate Dual-Stream** architecture (ETTh2 0.452, ETTm2 0.252), **not** the final
Residual-IA⁺ (ETTh2 0.346, ETTm2 0.188), and that intermediate architecture itself *loses* to
DLinear. P.3's own backbone-free Raw-MLP MoE in fact **loses to DLinear by +11.2% on all six
datasets** (Table `raw_mlp_moe`, Δ-vs-DL column): remove the TSFM and you fall *behind* DLinear;
it is the TSFM-inclusive Residual-IA⁺ that gets *ahead* of it. `[NEW]` We then ran the clean
isolation the reviewer asks for: Residual-IA⁺ vs. an identical-budget backbone-free Raw-MLP MoE,
holding the raw branch fixed and toggling only the backbone, at **H=192** (where the paper reports
the backbone contributes maximally). **Residual-IA⁺ wins 18/18** (mean −11.8%, range −0.3% to
−34.3%), including ETTh2/ETTm2/Electricity, the very datasets P.3 flagged as dead-weight at H=96,
while still matching or beating a 49K DLinear (seed-mean −6.6% to +1.8%). The corrected, honest
statement is therefore that the frozen backbone's contribution is **horizon-dependent**: small at
H=96 on linear-dominated data, decisively positive at H≥192, and "dead weight" holds only for the
pre-fix architecture at the shortest horizon.

*Generalization of the diagnosis.* Separately from the method, the **diagnosis is already
validated on nine datasets, not six**: beyond the primary six, RR-MoA is evaluated on Exchange
(R=2.17 → **−66.5%**), Solar (R=0.06 → **−32.9%**, the low-R outlier), and Traffic (R=0.14 →
correct **null**, +2.9%) (Table `exchange_solar`), with R(D) correlating with benefit at ρ=−0.88
(n=9). R(D) is an **a-priori** tool, computed from raw statistics before training, so it predicts
whether raw routing will help on any new dataset, Traffic being the predicted-and-observed null (a
falsification, not a failure).

*What we concede.* At H=96 on linear-dominated datasets the backbone adds little over a strong raw
branch, and ETTh1 at H=96 stays DLinear's on MOMENT-small (+2.2%, closing to parity by H=192). The
routing-collapse diagnosis and the training-free R(D) predictor, our core contributions, hold
regardless of which backbone is best on a given dataset.

let create 3 rebuttal responses for each reviewer based on the current unified draft: """Based on that email, the format is clear: **one rebuttal per review, not one big reply and not a separate AC letter.**

The email says "Per-review character limit: 10,000 characters" and "Use the per-review 'Rebuttal' buttons in OpenReview." So the structure is:

- One rebuttal attached to Pm4m's review (≤10,000 chars)
- One rebuttal attached to jemj's review (≤10,000 chars)
- One rebuttal attached to 8b2Z's review (≤10,000 chars)

There is **no dedicated AC reply slot** in this format. The AC reads all three per-review rebuttals — that's how they see your responses. So you don't write "to the AC"; you reach the AC *through* the reviewer rebuttals.

A few practical implications:

**The AC's 8-point list gets addressed inside the reviewer rebuttals, mapped to whoever raised each point.** The AC will recognize their concerns as they read. Memory (point 5), expert-scaling (point 7), normalization generality (point 8), task scope (point 3) → these mostly live in 8b2Z's rebuttal. Overselling (point 1) and (M,Σ) tension (point 2) → Pm4m's. Frozen-backbone (point 4) → jemj's. So by answering each reviewer well, you're automatically covering the AC's list.

**The "clarify any factual errors" invitation is used inside the relevant reviewer's rebuttal**, courteously — e.g., in 8b2Z's rebuttal, "we note the router input dimension does not grow with K (Appendix I.2)"; in Pm4m's, the SR-MoA "13–42%" referent. The AC sees these because they read all three.

**One nuance on the code-link rule:** the email says the *only* place a link is allowed is an Official Comment to the AC, and only if reviewers requested code. None of your three reviewers explicitly asked for code, so you likely have no reason to post a separate AC Official Comment at all. Don't create one just to "address the AC" — that's what the rebuttals are for, and a stray AC-only comment can look like an end-run around the per-review structure.

**Budget the 10k characters per review — that's generous.** Most rebuttals don't come close. Don't pad; the earlier drafts I gave you for Pm4m's W1–W6 and the two questions fit comfortably under 10k with room to spare. jemj (already a 5) needs the shortest rebuttal — mostly "thank you, here are brief answers to your four questions" — since you don't want to talk an accepting reviewer into new doubts.

**One caveat to keep in mind given the "no revisions" rule:** since you literally cannot edit the PDF now, every fix you promise (reframed abstract, promoted tables, corrected α wording, Figure 2 redraw) is a *commitment for camera-ready*, phrased as "we will…" — not something you can show them now. That's normal and expected; the AC can still write those commitments into the meta-review. Just make the commitments concrete and verifiable so they're easy to enforce later.

Want me to now produce the three final rebuttals, each formatted to fit under 10k characters and organized so the AC's points surface naturally within the right reviewer?"""

**Response to Reviewer jemj**

We thank the reviewer for the positive and careful assessment. Brief answers to the four questions, folding in the two weaknesses raised.

**Task diversity / Q1 (classification, anomaly).** [NEW] We ran RR-MoA on three UEA classification datasets (3 seeds): routing entropy stays healthy on all three (1.46-1.59, near the log 5 ≈ 1.61 uniform maximum, no collapse), so the anti-collapse mechanism is not forecasting-specific. Because frozen-backbone features cap absolute accuracy, we frame this as mechanism-generalization, not a classification-performance claim. Anomaly detection is a natural next task and we will add it in future work.

**Frozen-backbone requirement / Q2 (raw routing + selective unfreezing).** This already works, and encouragingly so: Table 3 shows RR-MoA (raw routing) beating the best fixed adapter not only frozen but also with Last-2 and Last-4 blocks unfrozen (ETTh1 -44% / -29% / -32%). Raw routing composes with partial backbone adaptation; frozen is simply the strongest configuration on most datasets (4/6), which Proposition 1 explains via a gradient co-adaptation feedback loop. Frozen is therefore the best-performing setting, not a hard requirement.

**Q3 (H∈{1000,2000}).** We test up to H=720, and within that range the frozen backbone does not become limiting: our deployment method Residual-IA+ still significantly beats DLinear at H=720 on the non-stationary datasets (ETTm2 -27.0%; ETTh2 also a significant win), while DLinear keeps its edge on short-seasonality data, so long-horizon behavior is dataset-dependent rather than a uniform degradation. The TSFM's contribution is in fact largest at intermediate horizons (H=192: 6/6 match-or-beat DLinear), with the raw branch carrying more of the load as H grows. Whether the frozen representation becomes limiting beyond 720 is genuinely open, and we will add the H∈{1000,2000} regime in future work.

**Q4 (training memory, raw + normalized paths).** Training keeps one frozen backbone plus tiny trainable adapters (354-466K, about 1% of the ~40M backbone) and the 853-parameter raw router (0.002% of the backbone). The raw path is a single univariate window, so peak training memory is set by frozen-backbone activations, the same floor as any frozen-backbone adapter method. At inference the whole stack adds only +5.9% latency and +6 MB (+1.7% of the 359 MB backbone; Table B.1).

We are grateful for the strong assessment and will fold these clarifications into the camera-ready.

input.content:
**Response to Reviewer 8b2Z**

We thank the reviewer for the constructive assessment and for highlighting the practical value of the signal-ratio metric. Several concerns are addressed in the appendices, which we agree we should have surfaced more prominently; we clarify each below and will do so in the camera-ready.

**W1 (memory of raw routing).** The phrase "routing on raw inputs" sounds memory-heavy, but the design is the opposite: the router reads a single univariate length-L window and is an 853-parameter Conv1d gate (0.002% of the ~40M backbone, 57× smaller than a 49K DLinear), adding <0.1 ms to the backbone's 52.9 ms forward pass. Total overhead across all three variants is +5.9% latency and +6 MB on a 359 MB backbone (Table B.1); peak memory is set by the frozen backbone every adapter method already loads.

**W2 (dataset-distributional / feature-asymmetry factors).** A fair ask. R(D) is in fact a dataset-distributional quantity, computed from raw statistics and predicting per-dataset vulnerability (ρ=-0.88, n=9), with Traffic (R=0.14) and Solar (R=0.06) the boundary/outlier cases; Appendix D.1 adds rate-distortion and information-bottleneck framings toward a broader account. We agree feature asymmetries beyond location-scale are not yet formalized, and our own ablations already show the operative routing signal is broader than (μ,σ) (App. F, SSR +48%); formalizing that is valuable future theory.

**W3 (scaling experts → router-input dimensionality / bandwidth).** In a standard MoE the router input grows with the expert count; here it does not. The router input is the raw window and is independent of K; only the K-way logit layer (64→K) grows, which is negligible. Because routing is Top-2, exactly two experts execute per sample regardless of K, so both active compute and memory traffic are O(2), not O(K). Table I.2 (K∈{1..10}) is the empirical stability check (within ±10% for K≥2). Expert count therefore creates no router-input or bandwidth bottleneck by construction; larger learned or dynamically-generated pools beyond K=10 are future work.

**W4 (other normalizers: BatchNorm / LayerNorm / RMSNorm).** App. H tests this interventionally: swapping RevIN for BatchNorm1d (entropy 0.62→0.004) and GroupNorm (0.51→0.000) yields identical collapse, while removing normalization keeps it healthy (0.82). [NEW] To match this rigor for LayerNorm, we also swap a LayerNorm into MOMENT's input-normalization position (same App. H protocol): it collapses identically (entropy → 0.000), with the no-normalization control healthy at 0.825. The apparent tension with our LayerNorm/RMSNorm negative controls (Chronos, Timer-XL) is resolved by where the norm sits: at the input position it strips per-window statistics and collapses; encoder-internal LayerNorm/RMSNorm do not strip the router's input and do not collapse. The rule is whether the normalizer strips routing-relevant statistics at the router's input.

**W5 (only forecasting / imputation).** Beyond forecasting on six datasets and imputation (Table J, 7/8 wins), [NEW] a classification mechanism-check on three UEA datasets shows routing entropy stays healthy (1.46-1.59, no collapse), so the anti-collapse mechanism is not forecasting-specific; we scope this to mechanism-generalization since frozen features cap absolute accuracy. [NEW] An input-length ablation (L∈{96,192,336,512}, 72 runs) shows no collapse at any L and raw > normalized routing at all 24 cells. Anomaly detection remains honest future work.

**W6 / Q3 (few epochs / convergence).** The complex dual-stream Residual-IA+ reaches its validation optimum early and overfits by 50 epochs; the simpler RR-MoA is robust to long training. Extending full fine-tuning to 50 and 100 epochs (90-config sweep) still loses to 15-epoch frozen RR-MoA by 33-71% (App. O). [NEW] We train RR-MoA to 200 epochs on ETTh1, ETTm1, Weather and Electricity (the dataset flagged as slowest to converge; 3 seeds each): routing never collapses (seed-mean entropy 1.02-1.34, minimum 0.87 across all 12 runs), and MSE is stable-to-improved versus 15 epochs (ETTh1 0.680→0.646, ETTm1 0.564→0.493). The reported 15-epoch numbers are conservative, not a convergence artifact.

**W7 (statistical corrections may be too conservative).** You are right that an over-conservative correction risks false negatives; we address both directions. [NEW] (i) Our claimed effect is correction-immaterial: the pooled Wilcoxon signed-rank on the RR-MoA-vs-best-fixed cells gives p ≈ 3×10^-11 uncorrected, so Bonferroni over every comparison in the paper still leaves it below 10^-9, and Holm/BH only lower it further. A per-dataset Wilcoxon with 3-7 seeds is limited by seed count, not effect size (an n=3 signed-rank floors at p=0.125), which is why the headline significance is the pooled test plus the 54/54 win-count rather than per-dataset p-values. (ii) The boundary null is genuine: on Traffic (R=0.14) RR-MoA does not beat the best fixed adapter even under the most powerful uncorrected test (+2.9%, p=0.88). We will report uncorrected and Holm/BH values alongside Bonferroni.

**Q1 (apply raw routing to an existing MoE, e.g. AdaMix).** We do exactly this. AdaMix-Raw swaps only AdaMix's hidden-state router for a raw-input router, leaving its experts and training loop unchanged: routing entropy recovers from near-collapse to near-uniform (0.49→1.55) and MSE improves 42-88% across all 12 cells. This isolates the router input as the dominant cause, exactly the clarification requested.

**Q2 (generality to image / other domains).** App. H.1 replicates the mechanism in vision: a ViT-B/16 with InstanceNorm1d on patch embeddings collapses (0.000), while ResNet-18 does not (its InstanceNorm2d strips statistics that do not carry the routing signal), matching the theory across modality.

Honest answer: **you can't "ensure" it, and right now these three are ~90% defense.** They're genuinely strong on the things ACs reward, but "the AC will like us more" is a higher bar than "we answered every reviewer," and there's one lever we're underusing. Let me separate what these responses already win from where they fall short *for the AC specifically*.

## What the AC actually rewards — and where we already deliver

- **We followed the AC's explicit steer.** They said "focus on 3–8 and clarify factual errors." All six technical points get substantive, evidence-backed answers (mostly in 8b2Z), and the factual clarifications are courteous. The AC will notice we did what they asked.
- **The "already in the submitted App. P" framing is the single best AC move in the set.** It reclassifies the AC's own point 1 from *"fatal overselling"* to *"a framing fix on evidence that was always there."* That is exactly what lets an AC write "authors will reframe; concern resolved" into the meta-review instead of hanging a reject on it.
- **Consistency across all three** (853 params, +5.9%/+6 MB, entropy ranges, the reframe) reads as a competent team, not three scrambling authors.
- **Every fix is a concrete `we will…` commitment.** ACs love this — they can enforce it in the camera-ready decision.
- **jemj kept short** so we don't talk a 5 into doubt.

## Where it's not yet AC-optimized

**1. It's mostly defensive, and it underuses the strength the AC already named.** The AC's own strengths list says *"novel with good causal analyses"* and *"the signal-relation metric carries practical value."* That is the AC telling you what they'd accept the paper *for*. Our responses answer concerns but barely reinforce that R(D)/diagnosis significance — and reframing (conceding DLinear) can, on its own, read as *"the contribution just got smaller."* An AC on the fence needs an affirmative reason to accept, not just the absence of reasons to reject. **I have ~3,000 characters of headroom in the Pm4m response** — the highest-value use is 3–4 sentences making the affirmative case: R(D) is a *training-free, a-priori* predictor that tells practitioners when raw routing helps *and* when to just use DLinear (the Traffic null), which is a general, transferable result independent of absolute SOTA. That converts the reframe from "we backed off" into "here's the durable contribution."

**2. The "this was a clarity/framing issue, the substance was always there" message could be crisper.** 8b2Z gave Quality 2 / Clarity 2 / **Significance 2** despite an overall 4; Pm4m gave Quality 2. The AC sees those low sub-scores. Every time we say "already in the appendix, we should have surfaced it," we're implicitly telling the AC those low marks are *presentation*, not *substance* — which lets the AC discount them. Worth making that subtext explicit once per response.

**3. The AC has to self-assemble the story from three disconnected documents.** That's inherent to the format, and the email's advice against a stray AC-only comment is right *for code links*. But it's worth **verifying** whether this track allows a short general author comment (many NeurIPS tracks do) — if so, a 4-sentence synthesis ("problem → diagnosis → R(D) predictor → deployment method beats DLinear 65:11, all in App. P") measurably helps the AC. If not allowed, we lean the synthesis into Pm4m's opening, since that's the response the AC will read most closely.

## The one risk to keep watching

The reframe must not leave the AC thinking the paper *was* oversold and is now just modest. The antidote is precisely the "understated, not overstated" framing — we're simultaneously **adding** the honest DLinear caveat the abstract lacked (fixes the AC's overstating concern) **and** surfacing the buried 65:11 (fixes the understating). Both directions are in Pm4m W1 now, which is right; just make sure strength stays the dominant final impression.

Want me to spend the Pm4m headroom on the affirmative R(D)/significance case (lever 1) and sharpen the "clarity-not-substance" line (lever 2)? Those two are what actually tilt an AC. I'd leave jemj as-is.

**Response to Reviewer Pm4m**

We thank the reviewer for the detailed, fair reading, and for noting that concerns, once addressed, would raise the score. We answer every point. All supporting results are already in the submitted paper unless tagged [NEW]; because the PDF is frozen, presentation fixes are stated as camera-ready commitments ("we will...").

**W1 (framing / DLinear).** This is the central point and we treat it as such, but one correction changes the conclusion. "Absolute forecasting quality below a trivial linear baseline" is true of RR-MoA-proper, the minimal diagnostic probe whose only role is to isolate the router input; it is not true of the method we deploy. Residual-IA+, already in the submitted Appendix P, does not trail DLinear, it beats it:
- 65 significant wins vs 11 losses (5.9:1); 107/123 match-or-beat (87%) across 6 backbones × 6 datasets × 4 horizons.
- 6/6 at the H=192 deployment horizon; MOMENT-large 23/24 with zero losses (16 significant wins); Moirai-MoE 15/15 (100%).
- It dominates on non-stationary data at long horizons (ETTm2 -27.0% at H=720; ETTh2 wins at all four horizons).
- Even at the single least-favorable slice cited (MOMENT-small, H=96), the net mean gap is -2.8%, a win, with ETTh1 the only loss.

We read the criticism as fair about our framing, not our evidence: we led with "5/6 match-or-beat" and titled the appendix "Closing the DLinear Gap," which foregrounded the one losing cell (ETTh1/H=96). We will (i) promote the full grid and the 65:11 win-count into the main text, (ii) retitle to the outperformance the numbers show, and (iii) reframe the abstract's DLinear comparison as scope, not deficit: "Because the router isolates the collapse mechanism rather than maximizing accuracy, the minimal RR-MoA probe trails a from-scratch DLinear on linear-dominated datasets; our deployment adapter Residual-IA+ removes this gap, matching or beating DLinear across six backbones and four horizons." We also accept the narrow, true version: RR-MoA-proper does trail DLinear in absolute MSE, sharpest on ETTh1/H=96, and we will introduce it plainly as a diagnostic instrument, not an accuracy claim.

**W2 (Figure 2).** Agreed. We will redraw Figure 2 at larger size with non-overlapping modules and a clearer depiction of the raw-router and frozen-expert paths.

**W3 (Moirai gains without collapse).** A fair distinction. Moirai applies non-learnable instance normalization (Kim et al. 2022, i.e. RevIN) to inputs/outputs, stripping the same per-window location-scale we study, minus the learnable affine. Raw routing recovers the stripped signal there by the same input-side mechanism, while the absence of learnable affine is exactly why AdaMix does not collapse on Moirai: the sudden collapse is driven by gradient co-adaptation and requires a learnable affine. The unified claim is "raw routing helps whenever per-window statistics are stripped from the router's input," and collapse is the severe failure mode that additionally requires learnable affine. We will present the cross-backbone results as consistent with the diagnosis rather than as uniform collapse-repair, and add the Moirai citation.

**W4 (heavy tuning; generalization beyond six).** On "heavy tuning": the 546-run sweep was development effort, and we agree it should not be presented as a SOTA search. But the outcome is not approaching DLinear, it is beating it (65:11), and the recipe is fixed, not per-dataset tuned. [NEW] Applied unchanged (gate-init b=-2, 5-epoch warmup, shared NLinear, validation early-stop) to three datasets it had never seen, Residual-IA+ matches or beats DLinear on 8/9 (dataset, seed) cells: Solar 3/3 (-9.5%), Traffic 3/3 (parity), Exchange 2/3, no collapse. A recipe that transfers to unseen data without re-tuning is the opposite of dataset-specific engineering, and answers "generalization beyond these six is unclear."

On "the raw branch does the work; the TSFM is dead weight (P.3)": one clarification we should have made explicit. P.3's "dead weight" verdict is measured against the intermediate Dual-Stream (ETTh2 0.452, ETTm2 0.252), not the final Residual-IA+ (ETTh2 0.346, ETTm2 0.188), and that intermediate architecture itself loses to DLinear. P.3's own backbone-free Raw-MLP MoE loses to DLinear by +11.2% on all six datasets: remove the TSFM and you fall behind DLinear; it is the TSFM-inclusive Residual-IA+ that gets ahead. [NEW] We ran the clean isolation directly, Residual-IA+ vs an identical-budget backbone-free Raw-MLP MoE, holding the raw branch fixed and toggling only the backbone, at H=192 (where the paper reports the backbone contributes maximally): Residual-IA+ wins 18/18 (mean -11.8%), including ETTh2/ETTm2/Electricity, the very datasets flagged as dead-weight at H=96, while still matching or beating a 49K DLinear. The backbone's contribution is therefore horizon-dependent: small at H=96 on linear-dominated data, decisively positive at H≥192.

**W5 ((μ,σ) tension).** The tension is real, and re-scoping Observation 1 resolves it: R(D) is the ratio of routing-discriminative variance in the instance-norm-removable component (location-scale) to that in the surviving component (shape), not a claim that (μ,σ) is the whole routing signal. When the ratio is high, stripping (μ,σ) removes most of the routing signal and routing collapses; when it is low (Traffic, R=0.14) the signal lives in the surviving shape, so stripping does not hurt and RR-MoA correctly does not improve. This is exactly consistent with the ablations cited: [μ,σ]-only routing degrades +48% (SSR) and temporal shuffling moves performance ≤3%. We will re-scope Observation 1 explicitly as a vulnerability predictor / lower bound, not a sufficiency claim.

**W6 (minor).** All accepted. The router parameter count is 853 (Conv1d 528 + Linear 325), matching the main text, Fig 2, Table A.1, and the released code; the Checklist's "~1.1K" was a stale rounding and we will correct it. On the SR-MoA figure, the referent is over RR-MoA (SR-MoA beats RR-MoA on all six datasets, Table F.2), but on rechecking that table the range is imprecise: we will correct "13-42%" to the exact 23-38% and keep the over-RR-MoA referent explicit. **Response to Reviewer 8b2Z**

We thank the reviewer for the constructive assessment and for highlighting the practical value of the signal-ratio metric. Several concerns are addressed in the appendices, which we agree we should have surfaced more prominently; we clarify each below and will do so in the camera-ready.

**W1 (memory of raw routing).** The phrase "routing on raw inputs" sounds memory-heavy, but the design is the opposite: the router reads a single univariate length-L window and is an 853-parameter Conv1d gate (0.002% of the ~40M backbone, 57× smaller than a 49K DLinear), adding <0.1 ms to the backbone's 52.9 ms forward pass. Total overhead across all three variants is +5.9% latency and +6 MB on a 359 MB backbone (Table B.1); peak memory is set by the frozen backbone every adapter method already loads.

**W2 (dataset-distributional / feature-asymmetry factors).** A fair ask. R(D) is in fact a dataset-distributional quantity, computed from raw statistics and predicting per-dataset vulnerability (ρ=-0.88, n=9), with Traffic (R=0.14) and Solar (R=0.06) the boundary/outlier cases; Appendix D.1 adds rate-distortion and information-bottleneck framings toward a broader account. We agree feature asymmetries beyond location-scale are not yet formalized, and our own ablations already show the operative routing signal is broader than (μ,σ) (App. F, SSR +48%); formalizing that is valuable future theory.

**W3 (scaling experts → router-input dimensionality / bandwidth).** In a standard MoE the router input grows with the expert count; here it does not. The router input is the raw window and is independent of K; only the K-way logit layer (64→K) grows, which is negligible. Because routing is Top-2, exactly two experts execute per sample regardless of K, so both active compute and memory traffic are O(2), not O(K). Table I.2 (K∈{1..10}) is the empirical stability check (within ±10% for K≥2). Expert count therefore creates no router-input or bandwidth bottleneck by construction; larger learned or dynamically-generated pools beyond K=10 are future work.

**W4 (other normalizers: BatchNorm / LayerNorm / RMSNorm).** App. H tests this interventionally: swapping RevIN for BatchNorm1d (entropy 0.62→0.004) and GroupNorm (0.51→0.000) yields identical collapse, while removing normalization keeps it healthy (0.82). [NEW] To match this rigor for LayerNorm, we also swap a LayerNorm into MOMENT's input-normalization position (same App. H protocol): it collapses identically (entropy → 0.000), with the no-normalization control healthy at 0.825. The apparent tension with our LayerNorm/RMSNorm negative controls (Chronos, Timer-XL) is resolved by where the norm sits: at the input position it strips per-window statistics and collapses; encoder-internal LayerNorm/RMSNorm do not strip the router's input and do not collapse. The rule is whether the normalizer strips routing-relevant statistics at the router's input.

**W5 (only forecasting / imputation).** Beyond forecasting on six datasets and imputation (Table J, 7/8 wins), [NEW] a classification mechanism-check on three UEA datasets shows routing entropy stays healthy (1.46-1.59, no collapse), so the anti-collapse mechanism is not forecasting-specific; we scope this to mechanism-generalization since frozen features cap absolute accuracy. [NEW] An input-length ablation (L∈{96,192,336,512}, 72 runs) shows no collapse at any L and raw > normalized routing at all 24 cells. Anomaly detection remains honest future work.

**W6 / Q3 (few epochs / convergence).** The complex dual-stream Residual-IA+ reaches its validation optimum early and overfits by 50 epochs; the simpler RR-MoA is robust to long training. Extending full fine-tuning to 50 and 100 epochs (90-config sweep) still loses to 15-epoch frozen RR-MoA by 33-71% (App. O). [NEW] We train RR-MoA to 200 epochs on ETTh1, ETTm1, Weather and Electricity (the dataset flagged as slowest to converge; 3 seeds each): routing never collapses (seed-mean entropy 1.02-1.34, minimum 0.87 across all 12 runs), and MSE is stable-to-improved versus 15 epochs (ETTh1 0.680→0.646, ETTm1 0.564→0.493). The reported 15-epoch numbers are conservative, not a convergence artifact.

**W7 (statistical corrections may be too conservative).** You are right that an over-conservative correction risks false negatives; we address both directions. [NEW] (i) Our claimed effect is correction-immaterial: the pooled Wilcoxon signed-rank on the RR-MoA-vs-best-fixed cells gives p ≈ 3×10^-11 uncorrected, so Bonferroni over every comparison in the paper still leaves it below 10^-9, and Holm/BH only lower it further. A per-dataset Wilcoxon with 3-7 seeds is limited by seed count, not effect size (an n=3 signed-rank floors at p=0.125), which is why the headline significance is the pooled test plus the 54/54 win-count rather than per-dataset p-values. (ii) The boundary null is genuine: on Traffic (R=0.14) RR-MoA does not beat the best fixed adapter even under the most powerful uncorrected test (+2.9%, p=0.88). We will report uncorrected and Holm/BH values alongside Bonferroni.

**Q1 (apply raw routing to an existing MoE, e.g. AdaMix).** We do exactly this. AdaMix-Raw swaps only AdaMix's hidden-state router for a raw-input router, leaving its experts and training loop unchanged: routing entropy recovers from near-collapse to near-uniform (0.49→1.55) and MSE improves 42-88% across all 12 cells. This isolates the router input as the dominant cause, exactly the clarification requested.

**Q2 (generality to image / other domains).** App. H.1 replicates the mechanism in vision: a ViT-B/16 with InstanceNorm1d on patch embeddings collapses (0.000), while ResNet-18 does not (its InstanceNorm2d strips statistics that do not carry the routing signal), matching the theory across modality.

**Response to Reviewer 8b2Z**

We thank the reviewer for the constructive assessment and for highlighting the practical value of the signal-ratio metric. Two framing notes upfront. First, many of the concerns are answered by experiments already in the submission (memory, expert scaling, other normalizers, applying raw routing to an existing MoE, a vision replication); where they were hard to find, that is a presentation gap, not missing substance, and we will fix it in the camera-ready. Second, where a concern asked for something genuinely new (an interventional LayerNorm swap, 200-epoch convergence, a significance re-analysis), we ran it, tagged [NEW] below. We address each point.

**W1 (memory of raw routing).** The phrase "routing on raw inputs" sounds memory-heavy, but the design is the opposite: the router reads a single univariate length-L window and is an 853-parameter Conv1d gate (0.002% of the ~40M backbone, 57× smaller than a 49K DLinear), adding <0.1 ms to the backbone's 52.9 ms forward pass. Total overhead across all three variants is +5.9% latency and +6 MB on a 359 MB backbone (Table B.1); peak memory is set by the frozen backbone every adapter method already loads.

**W2 (dataset-distributional / feature-asymmetry factors).** A fair ask. R(D) is in fact a dataset-distributional quantity, computed from raw statistics and predicting per-dataset vulnerability (ρ=-0.88, n=9), with Traffic (R=0.14) and Solar (R=0.06) the boundary/outlier cases; Appendix D.1 adds rate-distortion and information-bottleneck framings toward a broader account. We agree feature asymmetries beyond location-scale are not yet formalized, and our own ablations already show the operative routing signal is broader than (μ,σ) (App. F, SSR +48%); formalizing that is valuable future theory.

**W3 (scaling experts → router-input dimensionality / bandwidth).** In a standard MoE the router input grows with the expert count; here it does not. The router input is the raw window and is independent of K; only the K-way logit layer (64→K) grows, which is negligible. Because routing is Top-2, exactly two experts execute per sample regardless of K, so both active compute and memory traffic are O(2), not O(K). Table I.2 (K∈{1..10}) is the empirical stability check (within ±10% for K≥2). Expert count therefore creates no router-input or bandwidth bottleneck by construction; larger learned or dynamically-generated pools beyond K=10 are future work.

**W4 (other normalizers: BatchNorm / LayerNorm / RMSNorm).** App. H tests this interventionally: swapping RevIN for BatchNorm1d (entropy 0.62→0.004) and GroupNorm (0.51→0.000) yields identical collapse, while removing normalization keeps it healthy (0.82). [NEW] To match this rigor for LayerNorm, we also swap a LayerNorm into MOMENT's input-normalization position (same App. H protocol): it collapses identically (entropy → 0.000), with the no-normalization control healthy at 0.825. The apparent tension with our LayerNorm/RMSNorm negative controls (Chronos, Timer-XL) is resolved by where the norm sits: at the input position it strips per-window statistics and collapses; encoder-internal LayerNorm/RMSNorm do not strip the router's input and do not collapse. The rule is whether the normalizer strips routing-relevant statistics at the router's input.

**W5 (only forecasting / imputation).** Beyond forecasting on six datasets and imputation (Table J, 7/8 wins), [NEW] a classification mechanism-check on three UEA datasets shows routing entropy stays healthy (1.46-1.59, no collapse), so the anti-collapse mechanism is not forecasting-specific; we scope this to mechanism-generalization since frozen features cap absolute accuracy. [NEW] An input-length ablation (L∈{96,192,336,512}, 72 runs) shows no collapse at any L and raw > normalized routing at all 24 cells. Anomaly detection remains honest future work.

**W6 / Q3 (few epochs / convergence).** The complex dual-stream Residual-IA+ reaches its validation optimum early and overfits by 50 epochs; the simpler RR-MoA is robust to long training. Extending full fine-tuning to 50 and 100 epochs (90-config sweep) still loses to 15-epoch frozen RR-MoA by 33-71% (App. O). [NEW] We train RR-MoA to 200 epochs on ETTh1, ETTm1, Weather and Electricity (the dataset flagged as slowest to converge; 3 seeds each): routing never collapses (seed-mean entropy 1.02-1.34, minimum 0.87 across all 12 runs), and MSE is stable-to-improved versus 15 epochs (ETTh1 0.680→0.646, ETTm1 0.564→0.493). The reported 15-epoch numbers are conservative, not a convergence artifact.

**W7 (statistical corrections may be too conservative).** You are right that an over-conservative correction risks false negatives; we address both directions. [NEW] (i) Our claimed effect is correction-immaterial: the pooled Wilcoxon signed-rank on the RR-MoA-vs-best-fixed cells gives p ≈ 3×10^-11 uncorrected, so Bonferroni over every comparison in the paper still leaves it below 10^-9, and Holm/BH only lower it further. A per-dataset Wilcoxon with 3-7 seeds is limited by seed count, not effect size (an n=3 signed-rank floors at p=0.125), which is why the headline significance is the pooled test plus the 54/54 win-count rather than per-dataset p-values. (ii) The boundary null is genuine: on Traffic (R=0.14) RR-MoA does not beat the best fixed adapter even under the most powerful uncorrected test (+2.9%, p=0.88). We will report uncorrected and Holm/BH values alongside Bonferroni.

**Q1 (apply raw routing to an existing MoE, e.g. AdaMix).** We do exactly this. AdaMix-Raw swaps only AdaMix's hidden-state router for a raw-input router, leaving its experts and training loop unchanged: routing entropy recovers from near-collapse to near-uniform (0.49→1.55) and MSE improves 42-88% across all 12 cells. This isolates the router input as the dominant cause, exactly the clarification requested.

**Response to Reviewer Pm4m**

We thank the reviewer for the detailed, fair reading, and for noting that concerns, once addressed, would raise the score. We answer every point. All supporting results are already in the submitted paper unless tagged [NEW]; because the PDF is frozen, presentation fixes are stated as camera-ready commitments ("we will...").

**W1 (framing / DLinear).** This is the central point and we treat it as such, but one correction changes the conclusion. "Absolute forecasting quality below a trivial linear baseline" is true of RR-MoA-proper, the minimal diagnostic probe whose only role is to isolate the router input; it is not true of the method we deploy. Residual-IA+, already in the submitted Appendix P, does not trail DLinear, it beats it:
- 65 significant wins vs 11 losses (5.9:1); 107/123 match-or-beat (87%) across 6 backbones × 6 datasets × 4 horizons.
- 6/6 at the H=192 deployment horizon; MOMENT-large 23/24 with zero losses (16 significant wins); Moirai-MoE 15/15 (100%).
- It dominates on non-stationary data at long horizons (ETTm2 -27.0% at H=720; ETTh2 wins at all four horizons).
- Even at the single least-favorable slice cited (MOMENT-small, H=96), the net mean gap is -2.8%, a win, with ETTh1 the only loss.

We read the criticism as fair about our framing, not our evidence: we led with "5/6 match-or-beat" and titled the appendix "Closing the DLinear Gap," which foregrounded the one losing cell (ETTh1/H=96). We will (i) promote the full grid and the 65:11 win-count into the main text, (ii) retitle to the outperformance the numbers show, and (iii) reframe the abstract's DLinear comparison as scope, not deficit: "Because the router isolates the collapse mechanism rather than maximizing accuracy, the minimal RR-MoA probe trails a from-scratch DLinear on linear-dominated datasets; our deployment adapter Residual-IA+ removes this gap, matching or beating DLinear across six backbones and four horizons." We also accept the narrow, true version: RR-MoA-proper does trail DLinear in absolute MSE, sharpest on ETTh1/H=96, and we will introduce it plainly as a diagnostic instrument, not an accuracy claim.

**W2 (Figure 2).** Agreed. We will redraw Figure 2 at larger size with non-overlapping modules and a clearer depiction of the raw-router and frozen-expert paths.

**W3 (Moirai gains without collapse).** A fair distinction. Moirai applies non-learnable instance normalization (Kim et al. 2022, i.e. RevIN) to inputs/outputs, stripping the same per-window location-scale we study, minus the learnable affine. Raw routing recovers the stripped signal there by the same input-side mechanism, while the absence of learnable affine is exactly why AdaMix does not collapse on Moirai: the sudden collapse is driven by gradient co-adaptation and requires a learnable affine. The unified claim is "raw routing helps whenever per-window statistics are stripped from the router's input," and collapse is the severe failure mode that additionally requires learnable affine. We will present the cross-backbone results as consistent with the diagnosis rather than as uniform collapse-repair, and add the Moirai citation.

**W4 (heavy tuning; generalization beyond six).** On "heavy tuning": the 546-run sweep was development effort, and we agree it should not be presented as a SOTA search. But the outcome is not approaching DLinear, it is beating it (65:11), and the recipe is fixed, not per-dataset tuned. [NEW] Applied unchanged (gate-init b=-2, 5-epoch warmup, shared NLinear, validation early-stop) to three datasets it had never seen, Residual-IA+ matches or beats DLinear on 8/9 (dataset, seed) cells: Solar 3/3 (-9.5%), Traffic 3/3 (parity), Exchange 2/3, no collapse. A recipe that transfers to unseen data without re-tuning is the opposite of dataset-specific engineering, and answers "generalization beyond these six is unclear."

On "the raw branch does the work; the TSFM is dead weight (P.3)": one clarification we should have made explicit. P.3's "dead weight" verdict is measured against the intermediate Dual-Stream (ETTh2 0.452, ETTm2 0.252), not the final Residual-IA+ (ETTh2 0.346, ETTm2 0.188), and that intermediate architecture itself loses to DLinear. P.3's own backbone-free Raw-MLP MoE loses to DLinear by +11.2% on all six datasets: remove the TSFM and you fall behind DLinear; it is the TSFM-inclusive Residual-IA+ that gets ahead. [NEW] We ran the clean isolation directly, Residual-IA+ vs an identical-budget backbone-free Raw-MLP MoE, holding the raw branch fixed and toggling only the backbone, at H=192 (where the paper reports the backbone contributes maximally): Residual-IA+ wins 18/18 (mean -11.8%), including ETTh2/ETTm2/Electricity, the very datasets flagged as dead-weight at H=96, while still matching or beating a 49K DLinear. The backbone's contribution is therefore horizon-dependent: small at H=96 on linear-dominated data, decisively positive at H≥192.

**W5 ((μ,σ) tension).** The tension is real, and re-scoping Observation 1 resolves it: R(D) is the ratio of routing-discriminative variance in the instance-norm-removable component (location-scale) to that in the surviving component (shape), not a claim that (μ,σ) is the whole routing signal. When the ratio is high, stripping (μ,σ) removes most of the routing signal and routing collapses; when it is low (Traffic, R=0.14) the signal lives in the surviving shape, so stripping does not hurt and RR-MoA correctly does not improve. This is exactly consistent with the ablations cited: [μ,σ]-only routing degrades +48% (SSR) and temporal shuffling moves performance ≤3%. We will re-scope Observation 1 explicitly as a vulnerability predictor / lower bound, not a sufficiency claim.

**W6 (minor).** All accepted. The router parameter count is 853 (Conv1d 528 + Linear 325), matching the main text, Fig 2, Table A.1, and the released code; the Checklist's "~1.1K" was a stale rounding and we will correct it. On the SR-MoA figure, the referent is over RR-MoA (SR-MoA beats RR-MoA on all six datasets, Table F.2), but on rechecking that table the range is imprecise: we will correct "13-42%" to the exact 23-38% and keep the over-RR-MoA referent explicit. We will also remove the stray parenthesis in R(D) and standardize "fine-tuning."

**Q1 (input length 512 / horizon 96).** Horizon is already varied over H∈{96,192,336,720} (RR-MoA 12/12 vs best fixed; Residual-IA+ 6/6 at H=192). [NEW] We add an input-length ablation (L∈{96,192,336,512}, 6 datasets, 3 seeds): routing never collapses (entropy 0.98-1.48 at every L), raw routing beats the normalized-routing control at all 24 cells, and beats the best fixed adapter at 70/72. Conclusions hold on both axes.

**Q2 (α inconsistency).** Thank you, this is a wording slip. α is initialized at σ(0)=0.5 (the logit is a parameter at 0.0); 0.492 is the mean α at the end of the first logged epoch, after one epoch has moved it below 0.5, not the initialization (trajectory 0.5 → 0.492 → 0.468). We will correct the wording.

**On significance.** The durable contribution is the diagnosis and its predictor, and the reframing above sharpens rather than shrinks it. Normalization-induced routing collapse is a real, mechanistically-explained failure of the standard MoE-adapter upgrade on the dominant instance-normalized TSFM class. R(D) turns that diagnosis into an actionable, training-free tool: computed from raw statistics before any training, it predicts whether raw routing will help on a new dataset (ρ=-0.88 across nine datasets), and equally where it will not (the Traffic null, R=0.14, predicted a priori and confirmed). This go/no-go test transfers beyond our six benchmarks and beyond our specific router, since two architecturally distinct variants (SR-MoA and Residual-IA+) confirm the principle, and it holds regardless of which backbone is best on a given dataset. That, with the raw-routing intervention, is the contribution we ask the reader to take from the paper.

content.text:
The key to moving 8b2Z is reading their scorecard correctly, then knowing that 4→5 is mostly won in the **discussion phase**, not the written rebuttal.

## Read their profile first

Overall **4**, but Quality **2** / Clarity **2** / Significance **2** / Originality **3**, confidence **3** ("did not carefully check details"). Overall *higher* than the sub-scores + low confidence = a **sympathetic gap-lister**: they find the problem important (why overall is 4, not 2) but parked three sub-scores at 2 on "unclear / not discussed / limited" complaints. That is the *easiest* profile to move — every complaint is addressable, none is a fundamental objection. 4→5 is just a +1 "you filled the gaps" bump, the most common satisfied-reviewer outcome.

## Highest-leverage move: lift the Significance 2

It's the deepest anchor, and they handed you the opening — their own strengths list praises R(D)'s *"practical value beyond the specific method."* Convert that into significance by **reframing scope**: the diagnosis is not an LTSF trick, it's a **general property of instance-normalized backbones + MoE** — it reproduces under BatchNorm and GroupNorm (App. H) and in vision (App. H.1), and R(D) transfers a-priori to unseen datasets. They tagged the paper "Use-inspired" (narrow); every step toward "general phenomenon" lifts both Significance *and* that framing.

## Lift the other two 2s in parallel

- **Quality 2 ← rigor.** Foreground the falsifiable structure: eight causal controls, a predicted-and-confirmed null (Traffic), and the new interventional work (LayerNorm swap, 200-epoch convergence, W7 re-analysis). That reads as "careful science," which is what Quality measures.
- **Clarity 2 ← the "already in the appendix → promoting to main text" commitments.** You're explicitly telling them the low clarity is *presentation, not missing substance* — which gives them permission to raise it.

## Where 4→5 actually happens: discussion, not the PDF

8b2Z is conf-3 and admits not checking details. Such reviewers move with **consensus and AC framing**, not just your prose. Two consequences:

1. **The reviewers aren't independent.** If Pm4m moves up and jemj holds at 5, that emerging consensus pulls a low-confidence 4 toward 5. The *same* work that moves Pm4m 3→4 also helps 8b2Z 4→5 — don't treat them as separate battles.
2. **Be present and fast in the discussion window.** If the AC asks reviewers to reconsider, or 8b2Z posts a follow-up, a quick complete reply is often what converts "addressed" into "+1." A satisfied-but-passive reviewer defaults to keeping the 4.

## Honest odds

**~40% on the rebuttal alone**, higher if Pm4m also moves up and the AC nudges — because for a conf-3 reviewer, consensus does much of the work. The main way it stalls is **disengagement**: a reviewer who never returns to discussion leaves the 4 by default. **Response to Reviewer 8b2Z**

We thank the reviewer for the constructive assessment and for highlighting the practical value of the signal-ratio metric. Two framing notes upfront. First, many of the concerns are answered by experiments already in the submission (memory, expert scaling, other normalizers, applying raw routing to an existing MoE, a vision replication); where they were hard to find, that is a presentation gap, not missing substance, and we will fix it in the camera-ready. Second, where a concern asked for something genuinely new (an interventional LayerNorm swap, 200-epoch convergence, a significance re-analysis), we ran it, tagged [NEW] below. We address each point.

**W1 (memory of raw routing).** The phrase "routing on raw inputs" sounds memory-heavy, but the design is the opposite: the router reads a single univariate length-L window and is an 853-parameter Conv1d gate (0.002% of the ~40M backbone, 57× smaller than a 49K DLinear), adding <0.1 ms to the backbone's 52.9 ms forward pass. Total overhead across all three variants is +5.9% latency and +6 MB on a 359 MB backbone (Table B.1); peak memory is set by the frozen backbone every adapter method already loads.

**W2 (dataset-distributional / feature-asymmetry factors).** A fair ask. R(D) is in fact a dataset-distributional quantity, computed from raw statistics and predicting per-dataset vulnerability (ρ=-0.88, n=9), with Traffic (R=0.14) and Solar (R=0.06) the boundary/outlier cases; Appendix D.1 adds rate-distortion and information-bottleneck framings toward a broader account. We agree feature asymmetries beyond location-scale are not yet formalized, and our own ablations already show the operative routing signal is broader than (μ,σ) (App. F, SSR +48%); formalizing that is valuable future theory.

**W3 (scaling experts → router-input dimensionality / bandwidth).** In a standard MoE the router input grows with the expert count; here it does not. The router input is the raw window and is independent of K; only the K-way logit layer (64→K) grows, which is negligible. Because routing is Top-2, exactly two experts execute per sample regardless of K, so both active compute and memory traffic are O(2), not O(K). Table I.2 (K∈{1..10}) is the empirical stability check (within ±10% for K≥2). Expert count therefore creates no router-input or bandwidth bottleneck by construction; larger learned or dynamically-generated pools beyond K=10 are future work.

**W4 (other normalizers: BatchNorm / LayerNorm / RMSNorm).** App. H tests this interventionally: swapping RevIN for BatchNorm1d (entropy 0.62→0.004) and GroupNorm (0.51→0.000) yields identical collapse, while removing normalization keeps it healthy (0.82). [NEW] To match this rigor for LayerNorm, we also swap a LayerNorm into MOMENT's input-normalization position (same App. H protocol): it collapses identically (entropy → 0.000), with the no-normalization control healthy at 0.825. The apparent tension with our LayerNorm/RMSNorm negative controls (Chronos, Timer-XL) is resolved by where the norm sits: at the input position it strips per-window statistics and collapses; encoder-internal LayerNorm/RMSNorm do not strip the router's input and do not collapse. The rule is whether the normalizer strips routing-relevant statistics at the router's input.

**W5 (only forecasting / imputation).** Beyond forecasting on six datasets and imputation (Table J, 7/8 wins), [NEW] a classification mechanism-check on three UEA datasets shows routing entropy stays healthy (1.46-1.59, no collapse), so the anti-collapse mechanism is not forecasting-specific; we scope this to mechanism-generalization since frozen features cap absolute accuracy. [NEW] An input-length ablation (L∈{96,192,336,512}, 72 runs) shows no collapse at any L and raw > normalized routing at all 24 cells. Anomaly detection remains honest future work.

**W6 / Q3 (few epochs / convergence).** The complex dual-stream Residual-IA+ reaches its validation optimum early and overfits by 50 epochs; the simpler RR-MoA is robust to long training. Extending full fine-tuning to 50 and 100 epochs (90-config sweep) still loses to 15-epoch frozen RR-MoA by 33-71% (App. O). [NEW] We train RR-MoA to 200 epochs on ETTh1, ETTm1, Weather and Electricity (the dataset flagged as slowest to converge; 3 seeds each): routing never collapses (seed-mean entropy 1.02-1.34, minimum 0.87 across all 12 runs), and MSE is stable-to-improved versus 15 epochs (ETTh1 0.680→0.646, ETTm1 0.564→0.493). The reported 15-epoch numbers are conservative, not a convergence artifact.

**W7 (statistical corrections may be too conservative).** You are right that an over-conservative correction risks false negatives; we address both directions. [NEW] (i) Our claimed effect is correction-immaterial: the pooled Wilcoxon signed-rank on the RR-MoA-vs-best-fixed cells gives p ≈ 3×10^-11 uncorrected, so Bonferroni over every comparison in the paper still leaves it below 10^-9, and Holm/BH only lower it further. A per-dataset Wilcoxon with 3-7 seeds is limited by seed count, not effect size (an n=3 signed-rank floors at p=0.125), which is why the headline significance is the pooled test plus the 54/54 win-count rather than per-dataset p-values. (ii) The boundary null is genuine: on Traffic (R=0.14) RR-MoA does not beat the best fixed adapter even under the most powerful uncorrected test (+2.9%, p=0.88). We will report uncorrected and Holm/BH values alongside Bonferroni.

**Q1 (apply raw routing to an existing MoE, e.g. AdaMix).** We do exactly this. AdaMix-Raw swaps only AdaMix's hidden-state router for a raw-input router, leaving its experts and training loop unchanged: routing entropy recovers from near-collapse to near-uniform (0.49→1.55) and MSE improves 42-88% across all 12 cells. This isolates the router input as the dominant cause, exactly the clarification requested.

**Q2 (generality to image / other domains).** App. H.1 replicates the mechanism in vision: a ViT-B/16 with InstanceNorm1d on patch embeddings collapses (0.000), while ResNet-18 does not (its InstanceNorm2d strips statistics that do not carry the routing signal), matching the theory across modality.

**On significance.** We are glad the review already recognizes the signal-ratio's value ("predicting dataset vulnerability prior to training... practical value beyond the specific method"). We would stress that this is the paper's most transferable contribution: R(D) is training-free and computed a priori (ρ=-0.88, n=9), so a practitioner can decide before any training whether raw routing will help on a new dataset, and it correctly abstains where it will not (the Traffic null, R=0.14). Together with the collapse diagnosis it explains, that is a reusable result for the TSFM-adapter community, independent of which backbone is best on a given dataset.

Given that the memory, expert-scaling, normalizer-generality, task-diversity, convergence, and statistical concerns are now addressed, several of them from evidence already in the submission, we would be grateful if the reviewer would consider re-evaluating the score.

Use when 8b2Z acknowledges the rebuttal, or the AC asks reviewers to confirm resolution.
Reply within the discussion window: a fast, complete answer is often what converts a

## Primary reply — post if 8b2Z indicates concerns are addressed (or stays positive-but-no-score-change)

We thank the reviewer for engaging with our responses. To recap what is now in place: memory and expert-scaling are settled by the 853-parameter, K-independent, Top-2 design (active traffic is O(2)); normalizer generality by the BatchNorm/GroupNorm and [NEW] input-position LayerNorm controls plus the vision replication; task diversity by the [NEW] classification and input-length results; and convergence and statistics by the [NEW] 200-epoch and significance re-analyses. Several of these were already in the submission, and we will surface them in the main text.

Underlying all of them is one general finding: normalization-induced routing collapse is a property of instance-normalized backbones paired with a mixture head, not an LTSF-specific effect (it reproduces under BatchNorm, GroupNorm, and in vision), and R(D) predicts it a priori (ρ=-0.88). Given the concerns are resolved, we would be grateful if the reviewer would consider raising the score to accept, and we are happy to address anything further during the discussion.

---

## If 8b2Z raises a NEW point — open with one line of thanks, then answer from this fact-sheet

- **Memory:** 853-param router, +6 MB on a 359 MB backbone (+1.7%), <0.1 ms; the frozen backbone is the floor every adapter already loads (Table B.1).
- **Expert scaling:** router input is K-independent; only the 64→K logit head grows; Top-2 keeps compute and memory traffic at O(2); stable across K∈{1..10} (Table I.2).
- **Normalizer generality:** RevIN→BatchNorm 0.62→0.004, GroupNorm 0.51→0.000, [NEW] input-position LayerNorm →0.000; encoder-internal LayerNorm/RMSNorm (Chronos, Timer-XL) do not collapse. Rule: collapse iff the normalizer strips per-window statistics at the router's input.
- **Task diversity:** [NEW] classification entropy 1.46-1.59 (no collapse); imputation 7/8; [NEW] input-length 72 runs, no collapse at any L, raw > normalized routing at all 24 cells.
- **Convergence:** [NEW] 200 epochs (incl. Electricity, the slowest to converge), entropy 1.02-1.34, MSE stable-to-improved vs 15 epochs.
- **Statistics:** [NEW] pooled Wilcoxon p ≈ 3e-11 uncorrected (Bonferroni still < 1e-9); Traffic null genuine even uncorrected (+2.9%, p=0.88).
- **Raw routing on an existing MoE:** AdaMix-Raw recovers entropy 0.49→1.55, MSE improves 42-88% across all 12 cells — isolates the router input as the cause.
- **Vision:** ViT-B/16 + InstanceNorm1d collapses (0.000); ResNet-18 does not (App. H.1).
- **Significance / generality:** general property of instance-normalized backbones (App. H/H.1); R(D) is training-free and a-priori (ρ=-0.88, n=9) and abstains on the Traffic null.

---

## Tactics
- The 4→5 move for a conf-3 reviewer usually happens in discussion, not the written rebuttal — be present.
- If the AC asks all reviewers to confirm resolution, that is the moment to post the primary reply.
- Consensus pulls a low-confidence 4 upward: Pm4m moving up and jemj holding at 5 both help 8b2Z. Keep those alive.
- Keep replies short; link to tables; never re-argue a point already conceded or answered.
